stage_a.note: Very strong positive expression; she is vibrant, smiling, and energetic throughout the pitch.
Very strong expressed excitement; uses big gestures and speaks passionately about her culture.
Strong communicated warmth; she is very friendly, approachable, and considerate.

venture.description: Handwoven, colorful baskets and home decor made by artisans in Senegal to celebrate African culture.
venture.note: The founder is seeking investment for her e-commerce basket business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Sofi introduces herself, her background, and pitches Expedition Subsahara, a company selling handcrafted baskets from Senegal.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert expresses amazement at the baskets.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori asks if there is a specific purpose for each of the different basket shapes.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark opens and inspects one of the baskets.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Sofi explains they are modern vessels made with traditional craftsmanship, and points out the best seller used as a hamper.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond asks if the baskets are handwoven.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Sofi confirms that they are all handwoven.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks to confirm if they are made in Senegal and imported.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Sofi confirms yes.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori asks what the baskets are made out of, noting it reminds her of lanyard.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Sofi explains they are made from sweet grass, elephant grass, and recycled plastics for color.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark asks what it costs.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks how much a particular basket he is holding would cost.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Sofi states that one costs 18 dollars fully landed and sells for 50 dollars.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks how she sells the baskets, whether online or retail.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Sofi says they sell 95% online and shares that total sales to date are 900,000 dollars.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori clarifies if that figure is for this year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Sofi confirms it is for this year.

turns.speaker: PANEL
turns.summary: The panel collectively expresses surprise and applauds the sales figure.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Sofi adds that lifetime sales have reached 3.6 million dollars.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori asks what the sales were last year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Sofi answers that last year they did 1.6 million dollars in sales.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori acknowledges that she is selling a lot of baskets.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark asks what profit she made on last year's 1.6 million dollars.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Sofi states their gross profit was over a million dollars.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori expresses amazement.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark asks what her margins typically are.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Sofi answers that margins are about 60 percent.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark asks about her overhead and if she spends money on anything.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Sofi explains that the 1 million was gross profit and she reinvested quite a bit.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark clarifies, asking what her net profit was after the gross profit.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Sofi states her net profit was 75,000 dollars.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert reacts with surprise at the low net profit figure.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Sofi details her sales timeline, explaining the pandemic drop and the subsequent surge driven by the Black Lives Matter movement.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark tells her that is awesome.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Sofi explains how ramping up production to 120 weavers increased overhead, which dwindled her margins.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks if she is paying weavers a flat wage rather than on a piece basis.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Sofi says they pay them differently so they are her weavers, not the traditional piece way.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert challenges this, asking why not pay by the piece since productivity varies.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Sofi explains they take master weavers and have others learn underneath them.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks what the competition is doing.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Sofi asserts that the traditional way has done nothing for her community.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin points out that baby weavers will eventually become master weavers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Sofi explains they have to learn from a master to ensure people have a living wage.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark commends her approach.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks what she spent on advertising last year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Sofi says she spent 400,000 dollars on advertising last year.

turns.speaker: PANEL
turns.summary: The panel reacts with shock.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin notes that this is where the profit goes.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark asks for her sales numbers from the previous month.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Sofi answers that last month they did 160,000 dollars in sales.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond asks what her average sale amount is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Sofi states the average sale is 206 dollars.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark calculates the margins and asks how much it costs to acquire a customer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Sofi answers that it costs about 116 dollars to acquire a customer.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark points out that this only leaves her with 5 dollars.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Sofi agrees with Mark's math.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin states that it is a break-even business.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond asserts that she is losing money right now.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Sofi clarifies they do not lose money, but mostly just break even.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark asks where she sees the scalability of the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Sofi explains that because online customer acquisition is getting harder, she needs to move to retail.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert questions her desire to move into retail.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Sofi notes that she dislikes retail for tying up capital but feels forced by online acquisition costs.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin states he does not like retail for this business because it ties up capital, and he goes out.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Sofi thanks Kevin.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori loves the mission but feels the valuation is off and there is too much to figure out. She goes out.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Sofi thanks Lori.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark tells Sofi that she is in a difficult spot.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Sofi interrupts to defend herself, stating she turned 500 dollars into 3.6 million without a loan.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark believes she operates better as a sole proprietorship and cannot see a return on 500,000 dollars. He goes out.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert notes that she is asking him to make a bet on the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Sofi asks him to bet on her, emphasizing her extreme work ethic and dedication.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert says he would bet on her, but cannot see the return on a half million dollar investment. He goes out.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond disagrees with her statement about not accepting the status quo and decides he is out.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Sofi thanks Daymond for his time.

decisions.note: He does not like retail for this business because it ties up a lot of capital.
She loves the mission but feels the valuation is off and there is too much to figure out.
He believes she operates better as a sole proprietorship and cannot see a return on the investment.
He would bet on her personally, but cannot see the return on a half million dollar business investment.
He strongly disagrees with her statement about not accepting the way it has always been done.
